newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fewer New Zealand migrants in March - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: Fewer New Zealand migrants in March - SNZ.

text.p: New Zealand reported a net fall of 1,150 permanent and long-term migrants in New Zealand during March 1997, compared with a net gain of 490 migrants in March 1996, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.

In the March 1997 year the net gain was 20,940, which was 8,890 fewer or 30 percent lower than for the March 1996 year. SNZ said these figures included New Zealand residents returning after an absense of, or intending to be away from the country for, 12 months or more.
Overseas visitor arrivals in March 1997 totalled 149,080, up five percent on the March 1996 total of 141,420. This compared with a seven percent increase between March 1995 and 1996.
"After adjustments to remove seasonal variations, the number of overseas visitor arrivals increased by less than one percent between February and March 1997," SNZ said.
"This follows a one percent drop between January and February 1997."
In the March 1997 year, overseas visitor arrivals totalled 1.551 million, up eight percent on the March 1996 year total of 1.442 million.
